objectives: Define a contour line and contour interval
Recognise steep and gentle slopes, hills, valleys and spurs on a map
Calculate the gradient between two points
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify the exact conventions used in the Form 2 syllabus (V-shaped contours for valleys and spurs, intervisibility) and the worked gradient examples.

blocks.md: A **contour line** is a line on a map joining all places of the **same height** above sea level. The **contour interval** is the vertical distance between two neighbouring contours, for example 20 m. A **spot height** gives the height of a single point, and a **trigonometrical point** is a surveyed point on high ground.

blocks.caption: Contours of a hill
blocks.alt: Concentric contour rings with the closest lines on the west side.

blocks.title: Reading contours
blocks.md:
- Lines **close together**: a **steep** slope. Lines **far apart**: a **gentle** slope.
- Closed circles with rising numbers: a **hill** or peak.
- **V-shapes pointing uphill**: a **valley** (a river often flows in it); V-shapes pointing downhill: a **spur**.
- Evenly spaced lines: a **uniform** slope.

blocks.title: Gradient
blocks.md: **Gradient** = vertical interval ÷ horizontal distance, with both in the same unit. If a road rises 50 m over a horizontal distance of 1000 m, the gradient is 50 ÷ 1000 = 1 in 20 (1 : 20). Use the scale of the map to convert the map distance into metres.

A **cross-section** (profile) shows the shape of the land along a line: draw the line on the map, mark where it crosses each contour, then plot the heights on a graph. **Intervisibility** asks whether you can see from one point to another: if a hill is higher than the line of sight between them, you cannot.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not read the interval from the number of lines: use the numbers written on them.
- Convert units before dividing (all in metres).
- A gradient of 1 in 20 is gentler than 1 in 5.

blocks.title: Example 1: gradient
blocks.statement: A path climbs 40 m over a horizontal distance of 800 m. Find the gradient as 1 in n.
steps: That means a rise of 1 m for every 20 m along.

blocks.title: Example 2: which slope is steeper?
blocks.statement: Slope A has contours 1 mm apart; slope B has contours 5 mm apart (same map, same interval). Which is steeper?
steps: Closer contours mean the height changes over a shorter distance.
